column1: # The reviewed exceptions for the ZAP baseline scan (.github/workflows/security.yml).
# Every ZAP rule stays on, and the scan fails on any alert of medium risk or
# worse (.github/zap/gate.mjs), unless a line below says otherwise. Each one
# is a false positive or a risk taken on purpose, with the reason above it.
# Add a line only with its reason, and remove it once the reason is gone.
# Columns are separated by one tab: the rule's id, the action, and for
# OUTOFSCOPE a regular expression for the addresses (from their start) where
# the rule does not apply. The rule ids are listed at
# https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/alerts/
# 10055, Content Security Policy, on the public pages only. They allow inline
# scripts and styles ('unsafe-inline'). Every public page is built once,
# ahead of time and the same for everyone, and Next writes each page's data
# into it as inline scripts; a nonce, which would replace 'unsafe-inline',
# has to be new for every request, and so cannot be in a page built once. No
# public page shows anything a visitor sent. The admin, the one place with a
# session, gets a nonce and no 'unsafe-inline' (config/security-headers.mjs),
# and this rule stays on for it: the pattern leaves out /admin and
# everything under it.
# 10202, Absence of Anti-CSRF Tokens, on the admin's sign-in page only. Its
# form carries no token because the admin does not rely on tokens against
# requests from other sites: every admin route refuses one whose Origin or
# Sec-Fetch-Site is not this site, takes JSON alone, which a form on another
# site cannot send, and the cookies are SameSite=Strict besides. The form
# sends nothing itself: a script sends the password as JSON, and the plain
# form post a browser makes without the script is refused (415).
# tests/attack/admin-routes.test.ts and tests/http try each of these.
